patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — BigCommerce and Wix share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs. Choose BigCommerce only if your buying job matches “Open-SaaS ecommerce platform — Core $39/mo ($29 annual), Growth $105 ($79), Scale $399 ($2” rather than Wix's shape. Choose Wix only if your buying job matches “Website-first builder with ecommerce from Core — Light $17/mo annual, Core $29 (sell onlin” rather than BigCommerce's shape. Workflow advantage: BigCommerce leans wholesale-b2b; Wix leans checkout-conversion, website-builder-commerce. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — BigCommerce and Wix share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: BigCommerce is Open-SaaS ecommerce platform — Core $39/mo ($29 annual), Growth $105 ($79), Scale $399 ($299); GMV thresholds and open payment provider fees; Wix is Website-first builder with ecommerce from Core — Light $17/mo annual, Core $29 (sell online), Business $39, Business Elite $159 (annual tile.
- Company-size focus: BigCommerce (small-business, mid-market, enterprise) vs Wix (solo, micro, small-business).
- Workflow coverage skew: BigCommerce-leaning wholesale-b2b vs Wix-leaning checkout-conversion, website-builder-commerce.
- Researched limits: BigCommerce — 2026 GMV thresholds and open payment provider fees complicate TCO versus headline subscription; Wix — Website-builder commerce depth trails Shopify-class platforms on complex catalogs and B2B.

Limitations — BigCommerce: 2026 GMV thresholds and open payment provider fees complicate TCO versus headline subscription; Native POS/retail depth trails Shopify/Square for omnichannel-first merchants; Wix: Website-builder commerce depth trails Shopify-class platforms on complex catalogs and B2B; Plan gates for selling start at Core — Free/Light are not store plans.

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
